liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Reviewer recalls the Sugaree as epic; Sugaree and The Music Never Stopped are showcases for Jerry's guitar [17][18]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Reviewer says The Music Never Stopped rocks the joint [16]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): He's Gone flows seamlessly into Truckin' [16]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Fire on the Mountain is noteworthy [18]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Reviewer swears they saw a string section on stage during Terrapin [19]
- **Truckin'** (1 other source): A beat seems to be missing from the Truckin' intro [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd77-10-09 s1t01 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd77-10-09 s1t02 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd77-10-09 s1t03 They Love Each Other**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd77-10-09 s1t04 Cassidy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd77-10-09 s1t05 Dire Wolf**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd77-10-09 s1t06 Looks Like Rain**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd77-10-09 s1t07 Brown Eyed Women**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **gd77-10-09 s1t08 Lazy Lightning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-10-09.144481.sbd.troy.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 150 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1977-10-09.sbd.miller.109972.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 151 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd77-10-09.sbd.clugston.6954.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 152 min; rated 3.85/5 by 13 [6]. Said about its sound: Excellent sound with slight tape noise between songs; the reviewer rates the sound about 4.5; Garcia's guitar is over-distorted, particularly in the first set, though the effect becomes interesting once you get used to it; Sound is not bad and not distracting from the music [10][12][13][16][18]
- **gd1977-10-09.170284.set2.aud.tiffany.andrewF.flac2496**: audience recording; 10 songs; 92 min [7]. Said about its sound: Casey Jones is somewhat overdriven; the taper may have moved, or it comes from a different tape generation [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer, then 18 and washing dishes at a Denny's on Colorado Blvd in Denver, missed this show [11]
- This was the reviewer's first show, at age sixteen; they later attended Red Rocks in 78 [17]
- The music is loud and blasting, like most fall 1977 shows [10]
- The long, spacy Scarlet into Fire sounds much like the Birmingham show [13]
- Both sets follow the same pattern as other 1977 setlists, but the second set jams harder [14]
- Reviewer knew the 10/2 and 10/29 shows first; here both sets feature quick-turning jams and tight climaxes [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-10-09.144481.sbd.troy.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Sandy Troy; transferred by Matt Smith, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Sandy Troy's 7" Soundboard Reels @ 3.75 ips of unknown provenance (reels were not labeled, except to denote the date & dolby b) [1]. Also: Tape flips occur in Brown Eyed Women and He's Gone [1]
- **gd1977-10-09.sbd.miller.109972.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) [3]. Also: Tape flips in Brown Eyed Women and He's Gone; it may come from multiple sources; encore missing [3]
- **gd77-10-09.sbd.clugston.6954.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [6]
- **gd1977-10-09.170284.set2.aud.tiffany.andrewF.flac2496**: taped by thanks to Ben Tiffany for the source tape; source: Unknown AUD > ? > Cassette [7]. Also: Audience-recorded second set, with tape flips or gaps at He's Gone and at the start of Drums; Crossfades were not applied between tracks [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1977-10-09 Sun McNichols Sports Arena, Denver, CO](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1415107284362/grateful-dead-1977-10-09-sun-mcnichols) [22]
